title: After upgrading to 3.2.0.1 it is not possible to connect to a new pod (Omnipod Dash)
body:
getting the following error
Generic error: java.security.InvalidKeyException: Banned public key: 0000000000000............
![Screenshot_20231107-002749](https://github.com/nightscout/AndroidAPS/assets/148657741/5e46a5c9-1ddf-421e-bc2f-74a24fc08974)
![Screenshot_20231106-225212](https://github.com/nightscout/AndroidAPS/assets/148657741/42c88b37-0bad-44f5-854c-258170c7582f)
![Screenshot_20231106-224843](https://github.com/nightscout/AndroidAPS/assets/148657741/3e8298bb-58f5-49ce-b90d-e1e452b66800)

When I go back to my previous version (3.1.0.3) I manage to connect to the new pod and then again I upgrade to 3.2.0.1 and then everything works fine. But the connection itself with 3.2.0.1 failed
I tried resetting bluetooth, turning the phone off and on, reinstalling, clearing cache and storage, nothing helped. All I have left to do is go back to the previous version to connect and then go back to the new version.
Attached is the log in which the error occurred several times starting at 22:51:49.573
[AndroidAPS.log](https://github.com/nightscout/AndroidAPS/files/13273534/AndroidAPS.log)

> How can I check it?

You probably did, but just to make sure:
Verify your new version 3.2 was build with the same keyfile used to build your previous version 3.1.0.3

- When _updating_ version 3.1.0.3 to 3.2 by starting the .apk it should say "update" and after updating all your settings should still be there and AAPS running without you needing to do any additional configuration.
- Verify there is only one single AAPS app installed on the phone.

Yes
After updating to 3.2, there is no need to reconfigure, everything remains as it was in 3.1
And only one AAPS is installed on the phone

> Also a log of successful pairing with 3.1.0.x would be helpful

22:59:24.920 [main] D/CORE: [MainApp.onCreate():107]: Version: 3.1.0.3
Right after, the connection should appear

Ideally we would need a stracktrace (can be generated using AndroidStudio and your phone connected to USB), if you are willing to do that contact me on discord and I can walk you trough it.

Also with F21

> My phone is Xiaomi F21pro Android 11

This phone is not on the list of tested phones, known to work. Also, compatibility problems were reported with some Xiaomi phones in the past (Poco, Redmi).  As the F12pro is not on the list of tested phones this is likely is a phone specific problem or an issue with latest OS update.

Did you check with other users running the F21pro? Are they successfully connecting to DASH running AAPS 3.2?

The fact that AAPS version 3.2 was built on latest OS platform libraries libraries which could explain new compatibility problems with the newer version of AAPS.

**You can try:**
1. When activating a new Pod, disconnect all (!) BT devices (except for BYODA)
2. Disable any backgrond application that might use BT, disable any antivirus apps.
3. Uninstall AAPS, restart the phone, then re-install AAPS
4. Factory reset the phone to make sure there are no OS inconsistencies
(YMMV)

If none of the above solves your problem:
I's suggest to move to a different phone/brand that is known to work successfully with Omnipod DASH.

_Additional note:_
Omnipod DASH was designed and tested for the Omnipod PDM only. 
A lot of phones brands and OS's are able to connect and successfully operate with DASH, others don not. This is the why we have the list of tested phones: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1zO-Vf3wv0jji5Gflk6pe48oi348ApF5RvMcI6NG5TnY
But even then: there is a chance a tested phone will start gving problems because of an OS of driver update

Hi, thanks for the detailed answer, I personally know a few dozen people with a Xiaomi F21 that works fine for them with Omnipod Dash even with the new version so it can certainly be on the list of compatible phones, (I can also point out that some models of other phones that I know took the version 3.1 takes between 30 seconds and a minute to connect to the pod every time since 3.2 connects in 3/4 seconds) but it's probably a specific operating system version that causes this problem, I tried resetting AAPS as well as removing bluetooth devices and it didn't help.
